pages.title: From Physical Assets to Digital Intelligence
pages.heroText: Managing industrial assets is difficult when access is risky, inspections are slow and field information is hard to use. Birdseye brings inspection, reality capture, digital engineering and assessment together so your team can understand assets faster and make better decisions.

sections.title: Industrial Assets Are Difficult to See Clearly

items.text: Maintenance and engineering teams are under pressure to improve safety, reduce downtime and control cost. Yet important assets may be difficult to access, existing drawings may be outdated and inspection information may sit across separate images, reports and systems. The result is slower understanding, repeat work and avoidable uncertainty.

sections.title: Birdseye Connects the Full Information Journey

items.text: Birdseye is a Digital Asset Solutions company. We help industrial clients capture the physical asset, create a reliable digital record, turn the data into engineering-ready information and assess what matters for maintenance or investment decisions.
Safer access. Less disruption. Faster understanding. Better use of people and budgets. Clearer decisions.

sections.title: IDEA: One Practical Framework from Field to Decision

items.text: Our IDEA framework connects four stages that are often handled separately.
Inspect
Capture the asset, its condition and the operating context.
Digitize
Create point clouds, imagery, maps, models and structured digital records.
Engineer
Convert captured reality into drawings, CAD, BIM, as-built and other engineering-ready outputs.
Assess
Evaluate condition, compare change, identify priorities and support action.

sections.title: Choose the Solution That Fits Your Challenge

items.text: Every project starts with the customer's asset, risk, decision and required output.
1. Define - Agree the asset scope, objectives, constraints and required outputs.
2. Capture - Collect the required imagery, measurements, sensor data or 3D information.
3. Digitize - Create a structured digital record of the asset and its location.
4. Engineer - Convert the captured reality into usable technical information.
5. Assess - Review condition, change and priorities using agreed rules.
6. Deliver / Integrate - Provide reports, dashboards, datasets or system-ready information.

Birdseye supports Oil & Gas, Petrochemical, Power & Utilities, Maritime, Cement, Chemical, Mining, Steel, Infrastructure, and Water & Wastewater environments. Each industry page begins with the operational challenge and shows the most relevant solution path.
One connected approach from field capture to decision support
Remote access to difficult, hazardous and confined environments
Reality capture and engineering-ready digital outputs
Condition insight and system-ready asset information
Flexible project delivery across the Middle East, India, Africa and Europe
Technology selected around the customer's need, not around one manufacturer

pages.sourceTitle: Choosing the Right Industrial Data-Capture Platform
pages.seoTitle: Choosing an Industrial Data-Capture Platform | Birdseye
pages.metaDescription: A practical guide to selecting industrial inspection and mapping technology around the asset, operating environment and required output.
pages.title: Choose the Required Information Before Choosing the Technology
pages.heroText: Industrial teams are offered many drones, scanners, sensors and software platforms. The right choice is not the product with the longest specification sheet. It is the method that can safely collect the information your team needs and deliver it in a usable form.

items.text: Define what the inspection, engineering or operations team must decide. Is the need visual evidence, wall-thickness readings, a 3D model, a map, a volume, an as-built drawing or a repeatable condition record? The required decision and deliverable should guide every technology choice.

Consider whether the work is indoors or outdoors, confined or open, dusty or wet, hazardous or sensitive, and whether Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning is available. Access, lighting, surface condition, range, communications and site rules can all affect the suitable method.

sections.title: Match the Sensor to the Required Evidence

items.text: A camera may be enough for a clear visual review. Thermal sensing can reveal temperature patterns. Ultrasonic testing can measure thickness on suitable prepared surfaces. Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), photogrammetry and other 3D methods create spatial information. Choose only the data needed for the customer decision.

Good data must be linked to the correct location. Indoor or underground work may require LiDAR-based positioning because satellite signals are unavailable. Long routes and enclosed assets also require a realistic communication, navigation and recovery plan.

The platform is only one part of the service. Skilled planning, field execution, data-quality checks, processing, engineering conversion, technical review and reporting determine whether the result is useful.

Buying equipment can be appropriate for frequent, repeatable work when the organization has trained people, maintenance capability, procedures and enough utilization. A managed service is often more practical when the work is specialized, occasional, high-risk or requires several capture and engineering disciplines.

Birdseye starts with the asset challenge, required output and business decision. We then select the suitable combination of people, platforms, sensors and processing methods. The customer receives an accountable information service rather than an equipment recommendation alone.
Define the decision and deliverable first.
Match the method to the asset and operating conditions.
Include traceability, processing and reporting in the selection.
Evaluate the complete service cost, not only the equipment price.
Use technology as an enabler of safer, faster and clearer decisions.

pages.sourceTitle: Planning Commercial Drone Work Across Different Countries
pages.seoTitle: Planning Commercial Drone Work Across Countries | Birdseye
pages.metaDescription: A practical planning guide to the permissions, operating rules, site controls and data requirements that may affect commercial drone work.
pages.title: Plan the Permissions Before Planning the Flight
pages.heroText: Commercial drone rules vary by country, airspace, aircraft, operating method and project location. Early planning helps prevent avoidable delay and ensures the work is designed around the responsible aviation authority, site owner and security requirements.

items.text: Confirm the current commercial operating rules with the responsible civil-aviation authority. Requirements may include operator registration, aircraft registration, pilot competency, insurance, operating permissions and records.

sections.title: Check the Airspace and Project Location

items.text: Airports, military areas, critical infrastructure, cities, borders and other controlled or restricted locations may require additional approval. A site owner's permission does not replace an aviation or security approval.

Rules can differ for Visual Line of Sight (VLOS), Extended Visual Line of Sight (EVLOS), Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS), night operations, operations over people and different aircraft weights. The proposed method should be confirmed before dates are committed.

sections.title: Include Site, Safety and Security Controls

items.text: Industrial sites may require inductions, permits to work, method statements, risk assessments, radio coordination, hazardous-area controls and approval of the launch or recovery area. Indoor work may sit outside normal airspace rules but remains subject to site safety, equipment and security controls.

sections.title: Plan Data, Privacy and Export Requirements

items.text: Image capture, personal data, sensitive infrastructure, mapping data, radio equipment and cross-border data transfer may be regulated. Confirm how the information may be captured, stored, processed, shared and retained.

Permissions can take time. Include regulatory and site approval in the project plan, identify a weather and access window and avoid promising a flight date before the required approvals are understood.

Birdseye defines the operating concept, required permissions, site interfaces and practical constraints as part of project planning. Local approvals remain subject to the responsible authorities and asset owner.
Confirm current national rules for the exact project and aircraft.
Review airspace, site, security and data permissions together.
Do not assume an approval in one country applies in another.
Build approval lead time into the delivery schedule.
Use qualified local guidance where the regulatory position is unclear.

This article provides general planning information and is not legal or regulatory advice. Requirements change. Confirm the current rules with the responsible authority and obtain project-specific advice before operating.

pages.sourceTitle: From Preventive Maintenance to Better Asset Decisions
pages.seoTitle: From Inspection Data to Better Asset Decisions | Birdseye
pages.metaDescription: Learn how consistent inspection, digitization and assessment can improve preventive, condition-based and predictive maintenance decisions.
pages.title: Better Maintenance Starts with Better Asset Information
pages.heroText: Maintenance teams do not need more disconnected images and files. They need reliable evidence, clear locations, comparable records and a practical view of what requires attention. Digital inspection creates value when it improves that decision process.

items.text: Preventive maintenance follows a planned schedule. Condition-based maintenance acts when inspections or measurements show a need. Predictive maintenance uses trends and models to estimate when attention may be required. Most industrial organizations use a practical combination of all three.

Inspection data may sit in separate reports, folders, spreadsheets and systems. Locations may be unclear, terminology may vary and repeat inspections may be difficult to compare. This slows review and makes it harder to focus maintenance resources.

Use consistent capture plans, asset names, locations, viewpoints and measurement points. Link findings to imagery, maps, point clouds or models so future teams can understand where the evidence belongs.

Structure findings by asset, location, condition and agreed severity. Compare current and previous information, validate the results and give the responsible technical team a focused set of items for review and action.

Where practical, transfer approved findings into the customer's Enterprise Asset Management (EAM), Asset Management System (AMS) or Geographic Information System (GIS). The goal is to reduce re-entry and create a clearer link between field evidence and maintenance work.

sections.title: Use IDEA to Connect the Journey

items.text: Birdseye connects Inspect, Digitize, Engineer and Assess. The framework helps customers move from field capture to a usable digital record, engineering context, condition understanding and a clearer decision.

Choose a critical asset or repeated inspection where better traceability can create visible value. Define the decision, baseline, required outputs and responsible owner. Improve the workflow before expanding it across more assets.

Make every important finding traceable to an asset and location.
Use repeatable records to understand change over time.
Keep qualified technical review central to assessment.
Measure value through safer access, shorter review, focused work and reduced rework.
